Fourteen comments

Dandy Denny

A reel which in my experience is 100% associated with the North of Ireland. Bernie Stocks ( of “The Microphone’s Rambles” fame ) lived in Aberdeen for several years and gave me a tape once of various Belfast musicians, including Dermy Diamond whose main instrument at the time was the banjo. This was one of the reels played. I got the name of it from “La Lugh’s” CD, “Brighid’s Kiss” and the sleeve notes say they also got the tune from Dermy, who got it from Desi Wilkinson. A slightly different version was recorded by Frankie Kennedy on the 1st “Altan” LP. It’s the 3rd tune in a set of 3 reels which only gives 2 names. A simple tune, but with real drive in it.

↳ Posted by Kenny on April 16th, 2004.

Tape Worm?

Is Bernie the “Tape Worm”? I’ve been given numerous tapes of sessions around Ireland recorded by this fellow from the mid-80s and early 90s. Some great stuff. Tunes I’ve never heard on some of them.

Thanks for the tune Kenny.

↳ Posted by Phantom Button on April 16th, 2004.

Not Bernie

There was some discussion about the “Tapeworm” a week or so ago, and the answer would be “no”, Jack. Doesn’t sound at all like the Bernie Stocks I knew. Thought I should clear that up.

↳ Posted by Kenny on July 26th, 2004.

This is “Over the Water to Bessie,” isn’t it?

This is a cool northern tune, which I recently recorded from Radio Ulster’s programme Culan. The player is Ciarán Ó Maonaigh, and this tune is called “Over the Water to Bessie”: the same tune on “Altan.” I’m not really sure, but what Gian Marco posted on this site might not be the real “Over the Water to Bessie.” I need someone else to confirm this.

↳ Posted by slainte on March 18th, 2005.

Well, you can actually listen to C. Mooney playing this tune: http://www.rte.ie/radio1/thelatesession/rams/9january.ram The set starts around 24:00. What a player he is!

Re: Dandy Dinny Cronin

Hi Didier, that video isn’t the one I transcribed the tune from.

I transcribed the tune from a video that was Matt Molloy by himself, no accompaniment.

You seem to imply that I would post my personal version and claim it was transcribed from a famous player.

I would never do such a dishonest thing. I do believe I’ve been clear as to whether a setting is my own, or heard at session, or found in a collection, or transcribed from a recording.

Dandy Dinny Cronin, X:6

Setting from “Irish Tunes for The Scottish and Irish War-Pipes” - compiled by William Walsh, Chicago, Ill., arranged by David Glen, Edinburgh.
As a PS to Richard D, Cook’s post above, I may have made a false assumption about “Dinny” rather than “Denny”. I honestly can’t remember where “Dinny” came from, but at least 2 published sources have “Denny”, so I will go along with that and make the necessary amendments above.
PS - there are quite a few “unconventional” settings of well-known tunes in this book, which I will post out of interest in the near future.

↳ Posted by Kenny on May 9th, 2023.

Dandy Denny Cronin, X:8

This version largely tracks Gerry O’Connor’s playing with Lá Lugh off Senex Puer, though I haven’t transcribed the ornamentation. The recorded version also includes a number of variations, mostly swapping around phrase endings, but I kept it pretty straight ahead here. It’s a tense and haunting sort of tune that really lends itself to those little tweaks.

↳ Posted by j_clark on January 22nd, 2026.
